quotes.text: Your account might be reviewed after activation to confirm eligibility.
Recurring payments through Invoicing, Checkout subscription or setup mode, and saving Alipay details for future payments require access to the Alipay recurring payments private preview.
Stripe doesn’t combine the fields into a fixed descriptor such as `ALIPAY*MERCHANT`.

old_evidence.text: Chinese consumers, overseas Chinese, and Chinese travelers
CNY, AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, SGD, MYR, NZD, USD (depending on business locations)

If you have a bank account in another currency and want to create an Alipay payment in that currency, you can [contact support](https://support.stripe.com/email). We provide support for additional currencies on a case-by-case basis.
For connected accounts without standard Dashboard access, the platform needs to request the `alipay_payments` capability.

findings: November states 39 merchant-account countries, China customer-location listing, both domestic/cross-border coverage, B2B/B2C eligibility, Stripe and Alipay restricted-business checks, a post-activation review possibility, six explicit public-website requirements and ten prohibited MCC rows (new raw lines 18-70). May listed the same 39 merchant locations but characterized customers as Chinese consumers, overseas Chinese and travelers (old raw lines 16-18, 56-98). The new CN location field does not by itself settle customer-residence or traveler eligibility; retain the older wording as dated and qualify the apparent scope difference.

November expands the older currency mapping: adds CHF for Switzerland; EUR lists Croatia, Hungary and Liechtenstein in addition to earlier countries; GBP adds Gibraltar; USD maps to many listed merchant countries instead of only US (old raw lines 140-156; new raw lines 73-90). Both captures require an account bank account in a mapped currency and say customers also see CNY (old raw lines 140-142; new raw line 75). The old additional-currency case-by-case Support path is omitted in November (old raw line 158); keep dated, not assumed withdrawn.

The new access-type label 'Instant provisional access' and possible post-activation eligibility review describe merchant method access (new raw lines 12, 18-34). Payment confirmation is separately labeled immediate, while settlement follows the standard payout schedule (new raw lines 13-14); no claim of permanent merchant eligibility, completed settlement or a successful individual transaction follows from access alone. November also gives 0.50 USD minimum and 999,999.99 USD maximum transaction limits (new raw lines 66-72).

The standard capabilities matrix lists Alipay single-use, no recurring/off-session/setup_future_usage/Setup Intents, no manual or partial capture, no disputes, but full/partial refunds; PaymentSheet in-app payments are marked unsupported, whereas custom iOS/Android/React Native integration is explicitly allowed (new raw lines 10-11, 92-116, 139-166). The same page separately grants an invite-only Alipay-approved private preview for recurring Invoicing, Checkout subscription/setup and future-payment saving (new raw lines 168-170). This is a standard-versus-private-preview qualification, not a contradiction to erase.

Both captures retain 90-day asynchronous refunds, up to five minutes, failed/succeeded Refund status, and no standard customer chargeback process (old raw lines 132-138; new raw lines 108-137). November adds non-cancelable, never-reversal refunds, original source return, Dashboard/Refunds API tracking and signature-verification guidance (new raw lines 119-131). A submitted refund is not a succeeded refund; failed refunds restore Stripe balance and need another customer refund method.

November adds a five-minute Alipay authorization window, separate merchant-name/order-description fields under Alipay's display control, no guaranteed linked-bank descriptor, and PaymentIntent latest_charge.payment_method_details.alipay.transaction_id for reconciliation (new raw lines 172-204). On mobile the Alipay app or mobile site is used; desktop supports login or QR (new raw lines 178-188). Return is described after success, but reaching any return page alone is not outcome proof. No fixed ALIPAY*MERCHANT descriptor is documented.

Connect remains partial: destination and separate charges/transfers supported, standard-Dashboard connected accounts can enable; other connected accounts need platform alipay_payments capability request, whose API path is private preview, and direct/on_behalf_of requires Support access (old raw lines 160-170; new raw lines 206-214). Avoid reading the new broad Connect checkmark as unrestricted charge-type support. The mapped source's old 10-additional-currency/USD-US-only mapping and limited eligibility summary (source lines 13-33) require substantive correction; relevant index and concept at wiki/stripe-index.md:386-387, wiki/concepts/stripe-wallets.md:307-319 and wiki/companies/stripe.md:583-584 retain the older description and are context, not automatic edit targets.
substantive_changes: Expanded account eligibility with public-site requirements and MCC restrictions; explicit CN customer-country/cross-border fields and USD-equivalent transaction bounds (old raw lines 16-18, 56-98, 115-119; new raw lines 18-72).
New CHF presentation/mapping and materially expanded EUR, GBP and USD merchant-country currency mappings (old raw lines 140-156; new raw lines 73-90).

New capability matrix clarifies standard one-time versus invite-only recurring private preview, unsupported PaymentSheet versus supported custom native integrations, and authorization/capture/refund/dispute limits (old raw lines 32-54, 100-113; new raw lines 92-170).

New non-cancelable/non-reversal refund details, five-minute customer authorization window, descriptor/display qualifiers and Alipay transaction ID field (old raw lines 132-138; new raw lines 119-131, 172-204).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain May 2026 old raw provenance and the old Chinese/overseas/traveler customer statement alongside November's CN customer-location matrix, dated and scope-qualified (source lines 4-7, 19; old raw lines 16-18; new raw lines 62-69).

Keep the older 10-additional-currency/US-only USD map and case-by-case alternate-bank-currency Support statement as May historical facts, while the November map includes CHF and broad USD/EUR/GBP countries (old raw lines 140-158; new raw lines 73-90). Do not silently replace May history or infer any merchant account is enabled merely because its country is listed.

The old recurring approval requirement and Connect private-preview distinction remain, now scoped explicitly against November standard unsupported matrix and invite-only recurring exception (old raw lines 32-42, 100-113, 160-170; new raw lines 92-116, 168-170, 206-214).
conflicts: The November matrix marks recurring, off-session and SetupIntents unsupported in standard product support, while the same November page permits recurring Invoicing, Checkout subscription/setup and saved details under Alipay-approved private preview. Give reciprocal standard-versus-preview warnings instead of either absolute support or absolute prohibition (new raw lines 92-93, 149-170).

May customer audience includes overseas Chinese and Chinese travelers; November customer-location field says CN while also marking cross-border supported. These may reflect different identity/geography axes, so qualify rather than asserting all travelers are now excluded (old raw line 18; new raw lines 62-69).

May old currency table and source say USD only for US and ten additional currencies; November adds CHF and broad USD/EUR/GBP mappings. Preserve dated May scope and correct the current source to November mapping with reciprocal date labels (old raw lines 140-158; new raw lines 73-90; source lines 13,17,21).

New product support broadly marks Connect supported but the same capture restricts direct/on_behalf_of and capability API access; scope the matrix checkmark by charge type and connected-account access (new raw lines 149-156, 206-214).
unresolved_questions: How does the November CN customer-location field apply to overseas Chinese customers and travelers explicitly mentioned in May? The pinned overview does not define that identity/geography mapping (old raw line 18; new raw lines 62-69).
Does the old case-by-case Support exception for otherwise unsupported bank-account currencies still operate? November omits it without an explicit withdrawal (old raw line 158; new raw lines 73-90).

The exact private-preview API and account-specific entitlement for recurring Alipay are outside this overview; the invitation and Alipay approval are documented, but not verified for any account (new raw lines 168-170).

findings: Append November raw provenance while preserving May 2026 date and old raw (source lines 4-7, 35-37).

Correct 10-additional-currency and USD-US-only claims to a dated new map with CHF, expanded EUR/GBP/USD country coverage, bank-account prerequisite and CNY customer display; retain old map as May evidence (source lines 13,17,21; old raw lines 140-158; new raw lines 73-90).

Add eligibility website/MCC checks, method-access versus payment confirmation/settlement subjects, transaction bounds, one-time standard capability limits versus private-preview recurrence, custom mobile versus PaymentSheet, refund finality and descriptor/transaction-ID boundaries (new raw lines 12-14, 18-72, 92-170, 172-204).

Keep charge-type-specific Connect restrictions despite new Connect checkmark; require invitation/support and connected-account capability where specified (old raw lines 160-170; new raw lines 149-156, 206-214).
conflicts: Existing 10-additional-currency/USD-US-only summary conflicts with November expanded currency map; date both snapshots (source lines 13,17,21; new raw lines 73-90).
November standard unsupported recurring matrix versus its Alipay-approved private preview needs reciprocal scope wording (new raw lines 92-93, 149-170).
May travelers versus November CN location field needs an unresolved identity/geography caveat (old raw line 18; new raw lines 62-69).
source_assessments.reason: November adds material currency, eligibility, capability, refund, authorization and reconciliation information; the existing May summary is materially stale on currency scope and too terse for the new preview/product boundaries.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/alipay, the November overview describes a single-use Alipay wallet for listed merchant countries and China-located customers, with bank-account currency prerequisites, published 0.50 to 999,999.99 USD transaction bounds, restricted-business and public-website checks, and possible post-activation account review. Merchant method access is labeled instant provisional; individual-payment confirmation timing is separately labeled immediate, while settlement follows the standard payout schedule. Standard recurring/off-session/setup and manual capture are unsupported, while full/partial asynchronous refunds within 90 days and no standard chargebacks are documented; an Alipay-approved private preview permits specified recurring paths. Customer authorization has a five-minute window. Connect charge type, capability and business identity still constrain access. Old raw lines 14-54, 56-170 supported basic wallet, refund, preview and Connect behavior, but new raw lines 10-214 expand currency, capability and reconciliation detail. source-stripe-alipay.md reflects the May ten-additional-currency/USD-US-only map and needs a dated November correction. Enabling a method, returning to the merchant or submitting a refund does not prove payment settlement or refund success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/alipay, substantive changes include CHF and expanded EUR/GBP/USD mappings, website/MCC eligibility, transaction bounds, standard capability exclusions with private-preview recurrence, refund non-cancel/no-reversal behavior, five-minute authorization and descriptor/transaction-ID fields (old raw lines 100-170; new raw lines 18-214). Reordered tables and headings are presentation, while linked integration routes are navigation rather than execution evidence. source-stripe-alipay.md must retain May provenance and old customer-traveler and case-by-case-currency statements as dated, with reciprocal caveats against November's CN customer field and broader currency table. The new recurring 'not supported' matrix and invite-only Alipay-approved exception must both be shown; broad Connect support is limited by charge type, Dashboard access and preview capability. Distinguish custom native integration from unsupported PaymentSheet, provisional merchant access from individual payment confirmation, payment confirmation from payout, and refund submission from Refund succeeded. No account-specific eligibility, SDK behavior, bank-statement descriptor or successful payment is proved by this overview.
